subject: Re: Timeboxed pilot — wrap options and short extension structuring
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Peter Chu <peter@gleamanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: Timeboxed pilot — wrap options and short extension structuring

Hi Peter,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — we loved seeing your ingestion patterns. Attached is a short SOW draft and a usage estimate that maps your current test profile to a 2-week and a 4-week extension.

High level options so you can share with procurement:
- Option A — 2-week no-cost runway (limited to current rate limits; engineering support via async threads)
- Option B — 2-week credit bucket (50k token credit, refundable toward a committed purchase; standard 10% pilot discount)
- Option C — Paid 4-week extension at 30% off list with guaranteed concurrency for evaluation throughput

I've attached the SOW (placeholder) and a usage spreadsheet. If you want, we can also provide a short amendment for DocuSign once you pick a path.

Next steps: tell me which option procurement prefers and who on your side should receive the formal amendment.

Cheers,
Connor
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20260510-sow-draft.pdf (SOW draft), usage-estimate.xlsx (estimated token burn)
From: Peter Chu <peter@gleamanalytics.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Gleam Analytics procurement <procurement@gleamanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Timeboxed pilot — wrap options and short extension structuring

Connor —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. A couple quick clarifying Qs from procurement and our Eng lead:
1) For Option B (credit bucket) — does the 50k token credit apply only to generation calls or embeddings as well?
2) If we pick Option A (no-cost 2-week runway), can we request a one-time increase to concurrency for a two-hour soak test?
3) Can you share a short addendum template so our legal can review (we prefer to see DocuSign-ready verbiage).

We're leaning toward a credit bucket but need confirmation on scope and the exact discount applied to any subsequent committed purchase.

Thanks,
Peter
Head of Data Platform
Gleam Analytics
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Peter Chu <peter@gleamanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Timeboxed pilot — wrap options and short extension structuring

Hi Peter —

Quick answers inline:
1) Option B: the 50k token credit applies to generation tokens only in the current proposal — embeddings are metered separately. If you prefer a mixed bucket we can repurpose credits (we'd just need to adjust the economics; see row "Mixed bucket" in usage-estimate.xlsx).
2) Option A: we can grant a one-time two-hour concurrency bump for soak testing; request needs to be scheduled with Marcus (I cc'd him) so we can reserve the pool.
3) Attached SOW is intentionally short; Marissa can send a legal-friendly amendment template.

Proposed commercial recommendation (from our side):
- If you need procurement simplicity: take Option B (credit bucket). It preserves runway, reduces legal friction, and demonstrates performance.
- If you need deterministic throughput for validation: Option C (paid 4-week extension) with the 30% pilot discount and a performance SLA is best.

I can turn Option B into a DocuSign-ready amendment today if you confirm token scope and who signs.

Best,
Connor

Date: 2026-05-11T14:03:00Z
Subject: RE: Timeboxed pilot — wrap options and short extension structuring

Peter —

I'll keep this short. Commercial point of view:
- Pilot economics: Option B gives the best path to convert to a committed tier; we usually see higher conversion rates when customers have credits they can spend and then commit.
- Suggested amendment: 50k generation-credit bucket, embeddings billed at list for the trial, 30-day invoice net after conversion if you move to committed capacity.

Laura, can you prepare the DocuSign-ready amendment and a redline-friendly clause that limits the no-cost concurrency bump to a single scheduled window? I'd like to avoid open-ended resource allocation.

Peter, if procurement signs off on Option B I'll have the amendment ready and Marcus will schedule the soak window.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — procurement confirmed Option B (50k generation-credit bucket) and requests the DocuSign link for the amendment.

Action items from our side:
- We will sign the amendment as-is (please include the concurrency bump scheduling clause Marissa mentioned).
- Can you confirm the start date for the credit bucket? We prefer it to begin once the amendment is fully executed.
- Please include a point of contact for billing questions (name and email) so our procurement team can route invoices.

Connor / Laura — please send the DocuSign URL and I will have procurement complete it this afternoon.

Best,
